nodes.summary: A finite threshold equals `|W_j|` for some `j` with `W_j ≠ 0` that satisfies the defining inequality.
nodes.title: The knockoff threshold is attained

nodes.summary: If the knockoff+ threshold is a finite `T`, then for any set `H0` of null variables the false discovery proportion of the knockoff+ selection `Ŝ` satisfies `FDP ≤ q · #{j ∈ H0 : W_j ≥ T} / (1 + #{j ∈ H0 : W_j ≤ -T})`. This is the deterministic first step of the proof of FDR control, after which it remains to bound the expectation of the ratio by `1`.
nodes.title: The false discovery proportion of knockoff+ is bounded by a null-count ratio

nodes.summary: `flipSigns S w` is `w` with `w_j` replaced by `-w_j` for `j ∈ S`. The knockoff FDR theorems need only that flipping the signs of any set of null statistics leaves the law of `W` unchanged, the form in which Lemma 1 of Barber and Candès (2015, arXiv:1404.5609) and Lemma 3.3 of Candès, Fan, Janson and Lv (2018, arXiv:1610.02351) are proved.
nodes.title: Sign flip on a set of coordinates

nodes.summary: Under the hypotheses of FDR control by knockoff+, for `0 < q ≤ 1` the knockoff selection `Ŝ = {j : W_j ≥ T}` (offset `0`) satisfies `E[|Ŝ ∩ H0| / (|Ŝ| + q⁻¹)] ≤ q`.
nodes.title: Modified FDR control by knockoff

nodes.summary: Let `W : Ω → ℝ^p` be measurable statistics on a probability space and `H0` the set of null variables, and suppose that flipping the signs of any set `S ⊆ H0` of null statistics leaves the law of `W` unchanged. Then for `0 ≤ q ≤ 1` the knockoff+ selection `Ŝ = {j : W_j ≥ T₊}` has false discovery rate `E[|Ŝ ∩ H0| / (|Ŝ| ∨ 1)] ≤ q`.
nodes.title: FDR control by knockoff+

nodes.summary: The knockoff+ threshold (offset `1`) is at least the knockoff threshold (offset `0`), so knockoff+ selects a subset of the knockoff selection (Barber and Candès 2015, arXiv:1404.5609, remark after Definition 2).
nodes.title: Knockoff+ is more conservative than knockoff

nodes.summary: The variables `j` with `W_j ≥ T`, for the threshold `T = knockoffThreshold c q W`; it is empty when `T = ⊤`.
nodes.title: Knockoff selected set

nodes.summary: If the knockoff threshold is a finite `T`, then `(c + #{j : W_j ≤ -T}) / (#Ŝ ∨ 1) ≤ q`, where `Ŝ` is the selected set. This is the defining property of `T` (Barber and Candès 2015, arXiv:1404.5609, equations (1.8)-(1.9)).
nodes.title: The estimated false discovery proportion is at most `q` at the threshold

nodes.summary: For an offset `c` (`0` for knockoff, `1` for knockoff+), a target level `q` and statistics `W : Fin p → ℝ`, the least `t = |W_j| > 0` with `(c + #{i : W_i ≤ -t}) / (#{i : W_i ≥ t} ∨ 1) ≤ q`, and `⊤` if there is none.
nodes.title: Knockoff threshold

nodes.summary: A finite knockoff threshold is positive.
nodes.title: A finite knockoff threshold is positive

nodes.summary: Every variable selected by the knockoff filter (with any offset and level) has `W_j > 0`.
nodes.title: Only positive statistics are selected

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
